title: Relative Target Setting and Cooperation

scopes.description: Complete author-documented Stata workflow: exchange-rate/deflator preparation, annual and monthly variable construction, sample formation, Q/M peer-noise measures, cooperation measures, MIMIC model, target-setting analyses, and Tables 1–6.

requirements.description: Author-prepared annual business-unit financial and target data. The workflow joins by BUA_MODE/year and BUA/year and needs dept_id, year, BUA_MODE, BUA, actual and budget revenue/margin/cost/personnel measures, Currency, and restructuring status. FY2012 is retained for lag construction even though the final sample drops 2012; the datasheet describes company data for 2012–2014.

requirements.description: Author-prepared monthly business-unit financial data used to deflate and reshape monthly actual and budget values into calendar months, then construct monthly and quarterly peer-noise measures. Required fields include dept_id, year, BUA_MODE, Currency, and the 12-month actual and budget series for revenue, margin, and direct costs.

issues.description: The package inventory has no datasets. The do-file directly reads several author/company .dta inputs, including the annual and monthly panels and companion currency, third-party-revenue, industry-task, capacity/cost, capacity, and 2013/2014 hours files. Several have no producer in the supplied program, and no compatible delivery/schema route has been confirmed. This is an unresolved data/producer contract, not evidence that data are unavailable.

The program explicitly removes confidential code around country/business-group mapping and aggregation, irregular-unit sample exclusions, and table-output configuration. Exact upstream variable construction, exclusion implementation, and output path therefore remain unresolved; request the omitted procedures or author-prepared compatible intermediates and specifications.

The do-file mixes relative dta-files paths with S-drive paths and varies slash/case spellings for related BUA_Sample, Peers_in_Sample, and BUA_Temp intermediates. A future run can map the S-drive tree and relative dta-files directory to one chosen local root and normalize case as a supported configuration (A006); the current source does not establish that configuration.

The code imports a workbook named for NY.GDP.PCAP.CD, while the datasheet specifies NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.CD. Official WDI pages identify current-US-dollar and PPP products as distinct series. The intended product and workbook content are unresolved; do not silently substitute one.

The source names fields Longitude and Latitude and passes Longitude, Latitude, peer-mean Longitude, peer-mean Latitude to geodist. The command author's documented example uses latitude then longitude for each point. The required workbook is absent, so its actual column meanings cannot be checked; confirm the workbook contract before proposing a coordinate-order edit.

actions.description: Request compatible author-prepared annual, monthly, crosswalk, external-revenue, industry-task, capacity/cost, capacity-hours, and geocodes inputs with data dictionaries and delivery specifications, or ask the authors to confirm which files can be shared under applicable company restrictions.
steps: Ask for the exact author-prepared files consumed by the do-file, retaining identifiers, required keys, fields, units, and FY2012–2014 / monthly history.
For each file, obtain its producer/schema or a data dictionary that explains merge keys, field meanings, units, and missing-value conventions.
Use a compatible prepared geocodes workbook if available; the datasheet's historical Google Maps collection need not be repeated when that workbook is supplied.
validation: After authorized receipt, use bounded metadata/readability checks on each exact file and verify required keys, columns, and stated period.
Check the intended merge cardinalities and preserve the author-defined 2013–2014 sample and all listed analyses.

actions.description: Use the official WDI GDP-deflator product for 2010–2014 and prepare the code-required country/year aliases from it; use ECB reference-rate history for the separate exchange-rate input after confirming needed currency coverage.
steps: Obtain WDI NY.GDP.DEFL.ZS values for 2010–2014 through the official data/API interface; construct the CountryName, CountryCode, and year2010–year2014 fields required by the Stata workflow as a supported data-preparation step. The original 2015 workbook filename/layout is not required.
Obtain ECB 2012 reference-rate series for currencies present in the author BUA_Currency crosswalk; the Nigeria series remains a separate R013 requirement.
Keep the WDI deflator series distinct from ECB exchange rates and map each prepared source into the separate import contracts used by the code.
validation: After the confidential BUA/country mapping is available, check that the exact required country codes have 2010–2014 source values and that the prepared fields feed the author-specified lag and monthly-interpolation calculations.
Confirm ECB currency coverage against BUA_Currency, then inspect source sheet/header or API field mappings and reshape contracts before a future workflow run.

actions.description: Clarify the source contract for exchange11052015.xlsx because its NGR sheet is a separate required input from the ECB reference-rate file.
steps: Ask the authors for the workbook provider/source, the NGR series definition and units, the RateYear range, and the correct 2012 exchange-rate value/conversion direction.
Request the exact compatible workbook or an author-prepared series with the same fields.
validation: After confirmation, verify the NGR and RateYear columns and the year range with a bounded workbook inspection.

actions.description: Ask the authors to resolve the GDP-per-capita indicator discrepancy before choosing a public product or changing either import branch.
steps: Confirm whether the intended series is NY.GDP.PCAP.CD (current US dollars) or NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.CD (current international dollars), and provide or identify the original 2012–2014 workbook.
Confirm the omitted BUA_MODE/country mapping and whether both GDP_Growth branches should use the same series.
validation: Verify the selected workbook's product code, 2012–2014 values, and imported column positions against the confirmed author specification.
If a source edit is required, keep the selection consistent in both import branches and preserve the 2013/2014 growth formulas.

review_notes: The release contains substantial executable Stata preparation and analysis code; the only entry point is the supplied do-file. No companion analysis program or usable final BUA_Temp.dta is supplied.

No analysis_only scope is supported: the data-analysis section reads BUA_Temp.dta after earlier construction, but this author-prepared analysis dataset is not present and no compatible route to it is verified.

The script itself specifies the Q and M period branches, 1/99 trims, MIMIC mlmv models, robust variants, controls, sample rules, and all Table 1–6 analyses. These settings are retained. Data-derived sample counts are unknown and are not invented.
All 26 frozen dependency IDs have explicit reviews. Manual source scanning also found BUA_Currency, BUA_Hours_3rdP_Rev, BUA_Capacity_Cost, and BUA_Capacity reads not represented by the checklist.
Stata18 self-written synthetic-file evidence confirms use with replace is accepted in this runtime; no repair is proposed for that line.

The browse call displays peer counts; no manual selection result is consumed by later code. A compatible prepared geocodes workbook can serve as the primary input route without repeating the historical Google Maps lookup.

The relative/S-drive and BUA_Temp case variations are addressable through one chosen local-root configuration and case normalization (A006); this is a supported setup step, not an author clarification. The final table-output directory and confidential mapping steps remain unresolved under I002.
